title: Why Anyone Still Walks
summary: Nobody on Tessell can design a battlemech. What they can do is cut one apart and build it back wrong.
body: The Compact left depots. Not machines — hulls. Frames on their sides in the dark, spares crated by a numbering system nobody kept the key to, and the automated foundries at Sarn that will still take an order if you can pay the power bill and wait out the queue.

So no mech on Tessell is new, and none is original. You pull a Compact hull out of a depot, cut what has seized, re-armour it in Sarn plate, hang whatever guns the smelter towns can still turn out, and stamp it with a mark number that means only how many times it has been through the shop.

This is why two machines on the same chassis can be nothing alike, why a lance that loses a mech does not simply order another, and why the most valuable thing on any battlefield is the wreck that is still standing at the end of it.
Take the legs and you get the chassis. Take the centre torso and you get scrap and a funeral.
